Sean / team —

Quick engineering numbers (assumptions: T4x2-like node with optimized kernels, avg 120 tokens/request, 16-token prompt overhead, continuous batching windows ~30ms):

• Single GPU steady qps (sustained small requests): ~110–130 qps (conservative: 110).
• Single GPU burst envelope (short windows, aggressive batching): up to ~300 qps for ~30–60s before thermal throttles/queueing show.
• Cache warmup: cold-to-steady for common prefixes ~60–120s depending on request diversity; KV cache rebuild after restart ~2–4 minutes for useful hit rates.
• Network egress: at 120 tokens/request and average token size 2 bytes (post-compression), 800 qps ≈ 1.9 Gbps egress baseline; 3x burst ≈ 5.7 Gbps — fits their 10 Gbps cap but leaves limited headroom for other traffic.
• Sizing: to hit 800 steady qps with a conservative 110 qps/GPU -> 8 GPUs (reserve 1 for safety = 9). For 3x burst absorb (without autoscaling) we'd need 24–27 GPUs; with burst autoscale + admission control, commit to 12 GPUs + warm pool + fast scale to 20 GPUs within 90s.

Failure-mode checklist (engineering highlights):
- Pod-level GPU OOM: ensure pod eviction policy & per-request input-size caps; automated retry to fallbacks.
- NIC flap: route failover to standby subnet + short-lived queueing with priority for warm-cached requests.
- KV cache cold start: pre-warm critical prefixes during planned increases; maintain a lightweight sampler to prime caches on scale events.
- Disk-backed cache fallback: if in-memory cache rebuilding exceeds 3min, route to disk-backed read path (slower but prevents full cold misses).

I'll attach a short workbook mapping QPS to GPU counts with these assumptions.

—Jonas
Senior Systems Engineer, Redwood Inference

Jason —

Appended is a concise plan and attachments (atlas_capacity_model_v1.xlsx, network_topology_vpc.svg, privgpu-failure-mode-checklist.pdf). TL;DR recommendations:

1) Sizing: baseline commit = 9 GPUs to hit 800 qps steady. For 3x short bursts, either commit 24 GPUs or adopt burst autoscale. Recommended commercial approach: commit to 12 GPUs + warm pool policy + autoscale to 20 GPUs (scale window target 60–90s).
2) Network: your 10 Gbps egress cap is workable but tight during bursts — plan to reserve 2–3 Gbps for non-inference traffic or request a temporary lift for launch windows.
3) Warmup: maintain 15% pre-warmed capacity during business hours and run an automated prefix sampler that primes top-200 prefixes on scale events (expect useful cache rebuild in 2–4 minutes).
4) Operational runbook & failure modes: we provided a 1-page checklist that flags when to: (a) run cache warmers, (b) initiate emergency scale, (c) flip to degraded routing (smaller models) to preserve latency.
